Winetricks is a very useful helper script for managing Wineprefixes, as it grants you a command line tool (and GUI interface) for easily installing additional components and fonts often required to get a Windows application (including Games) working correctly.

Unfortunately, many distros do not include Winetricks within the Wine package, as it is a separate project and is often used to replace components created by the Wine Project, with closed source counterparts, in order to get an application working.

Even if you end up not using Winetricks for this reason, it is often a good idea to install it, because you never know.

Note: You can also install Winetricks using your distro's package manager GUI front-end. But installing from the terminal is faster. Let's be honest.

Arch Linux (Arch Based Distributions)

Winetricks is available in the Arch Repositories (the git version is also available in the AUR). To install Winetricks from the Arch Repositories:

sudo pacman -S winetricks

Ubuntu Linux (Ubuntu Based Distributions)

Winetricks is included in the Ubuntu Repositories, so installing it is as simple as opening the terminal and typing:

sudo apt install winetricks

Solus Linux

Winetricks is available in the Solus Repositories. Use the following command to install:

sudo eopkg install winetricks
